doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Carnegie Hall revivals and Gallodoro finding his own handwriting in Whiteman parts
summary: Willcox did the Goldkette revival and Gallodoro the Paul Whiteman Rediscovered concerts around 1977; Gallodoro recognises his own markings on music borrowed from Williams College.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Now you both got to do a kind of a revival thing at Carnegie Hall, right?
But he did the Goldkette group.

I did the Paul Whiteman Rediscovered. Around 1977. We opened at the Academy of Music in Philadelphia, standing room, two days later we went to Carnegie Hall, standing room, we were supposed to go on the road and nothing happened. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

I think I told you this before. Dick Sudhalter had borrowed some of the music from Williams College, because Whiteman donated all of his music there. So “Last Night on the Back Porch” or one of those tunes, rehearsing, out of, all of a sudden I seen my handwriting about from here to here, a p, double p here, double forte here, you know you can’t miss your own handwriting.
That back porch tune was written by a guy from Cornell.
Yes. I can’t think of his name.
Oh, it’s such a small world in the music business. For you to get that music back in front of you after all those years and see your own handwriting on it. That’s very interesting.
